runtimeKernelsNote: kernel_selection_contract_v1 registry, extended in Phase P1C from the single P1B baseline candidate to a frozen 8-candidate tile/schedule family for the same fused_matmul_bias_relu op (identical semantics, dtype f32, backend cpu, one thread, same compiler flags -- only block_m/block_n/block_k differ; see DOC/result/P1C_*.md for the full working-set-vs-Cortex-A76-cache rationale). bm32_bn32_bk32 remains declared FIRST for exact backward compatibility with the accepted P1B behavior. IMPORTANT, VERIFIED ARCHITECTURAL LIMITATION (audited in Phase P1C, not fabricated): KernelSelectionPass matches candidates on (op_name, backend, dtype, quant_mode, layout, tile-plan, local-memory) and picks the FIRST full match in declaration order, short-circuiting the search -- it has NO signal that varies with an op's concrete (M,N,K) shape, so it cannot and does not perform shape-aware or cache-aware candidate selection today. Declaring a supportedTileShapes constraint per candidate would not fix this: TilePlanningPass never produces a tile plan on this profile (staticCostProfile.localMemoryBytes is deliberately undeclared, per the P1A decision that this Cortex-A76's hardware-managed cache is not a software-managed scratchpad), so every candidate's tile-shape check would defer (deferred_missing_tile_plan) rather than select. Consequently: for ANY workload shape, this profile's live compiler selection is, and will remain, bm32_bn32_bk32 -- the other 7 candidates are declared (so Runtime can recognize and dispatch them, and so P1C's oracle/regret measurement can invoke them directly) but are NOT reachable through today's live KernelSelectionPass for any input shape. The candidate-space discovery, oracle comparison, and any calibrated-policy evaluation in Phase P1C were therefore performed by invoking Runtime directly with each declared candidate ID, the same methodology Phase 1/R1's CPU schedule-discovery tool already used, independent of live compiler selection. This is a real, verified gap, documented here rather than worked around by fabricating shape-aware pass logic in this phase. The schema/pass also cannot retain 'candidates considered but not selected' when a match succeeds (the match loop breaks on the first full match), so only the winning descriptor's identity is ever exported in kernel_selection.* -- also documented here rather than fabricated. ml-platform-capabilities is not consulted by this declaration (existing architectural bypass predating P1B, unchanged here).
